concepts.label: vBucket failover log
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the per-vBucket log of {id, seq} entries this command exposes, one mechanism-level concept for the whole page rather than a concept per field (id/seq/num_entries), per this round's explicit warning against minting a concept per table row on a table-shaped dump. Placed in vbucket: alongside vbucket:checkpoint (also minted this batch) since it is per-vBucket state, distinct from the server:failover action itself.

notable_absence.finding: This is the thinnest page in the batch: description is 'This command provides information about entries such as IDs, sequence, and number' and the example gives only raw field:value pairs (vb_N:0:id, vb_N:0:seq, vb_N:num_entries) with zero prose explaining what an 'entry' represents (e.g. a vBucket-UUID/high-seqno pair recorded at each failover event) or which other mechanism - DCP stream negotiation, server:failover itself - reads this log. No quotable sentence supports any relation, so none is asserted rather than reconstructed.

cross_component_finding: No relation is quotable from this page alone, but its field vocabulary (per-vBucket id/seq pairs) parallels the vb_uuid field cbstats-dcp.md's stream tables use for DCP stream creation - consistent with a failover log being what DCP consults to negotiate a resuming stream after a topology change - though the page itself states no such connection, so this is recorded as a finding only, not a relation.
cross_product_finding: Not applicable - no cross-product vocabulary is stated or implied on this page.
